entries.title: Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know

entries.title: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
entries.snippet: The U.S. birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The drop would have been greater, but women over age 30 are having more children.

entries.title: This decade has been missing its big-impact midterm
entries.snippet: Every other decade over the past hundred years has produced at least one midterm that made a big difference in Congress and in national politics more broadly.

entries.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
entries.snippet: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.

entries.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
entries.snippet: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

entries.title: Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms
entries.snippet: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.

entries.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
entries.snippet: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

entries.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
entries.snippet: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.

entries.title: Rollins says USDA is 'full-bore ahead' on Forest Service reorganization
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to move Forest Service headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City, shutter 23 research stations, and close many regional offices and replace them with state offices.

entries.title: Signs of fraying loyalty emerge in Netanyahu stronghold before Israeli election
entries.snippet: Kiryat Shmona, Israel's northernmost city, has long been a bastion of support for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party. But that loyalty is no longer ironclad.

entries.title: Treasury proposes rule to curb high-tech investments in China and other adversaries
entries.snippet: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern."

entries.title: Defense attorneys in case over Charlie Kirk's killing say they need years to prepare for trial
entries.snippet: Defense attorneys for the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk are suggesting a 2029 trial date because they say it could take them that long to prepare their case.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump at GOP rally in Florida revives idea of military intervention in Cuba after Iran
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country.

entries.title: Oregon father who killed school shooter says he regrets there were children he didn't save
entries.snippet: Kaylub Giamanco, whose two daughters attend Silver Rail Elementary, where the Oct. 15 attack occurred, said he was the children's "last line of defense" and that he regrets not arriving soon enough to save them all.

entries.title: Why experts are pushing RFK Jr. to release a federal definition of ultraprocessed foods
entries.snippet: More than 100 science, medical and nutrition experts signed and sent an open letter Friday to the Office of Management and Budget, urging the administration to release the first-ever government definition of ultraprocessed foods.

entries.title: DOJ has monitored elections for decades. Here's why some state officials are concerned this year
entries.snippet: The agency regularly monitors polling places. But this year's effort on Nov. 3 will more than double the number of federal monitors deployed during the 2022 midterms.

entries.title: Police officer who shot and killed 1-year-old boy in Mississippi has resigned, mayor says
entries.snippet: Sgt. Hunter Foster, 33, had been cleared of criminal wrongdoing by the Mississippi Attorney General's office earlier this week after its monthslong probe concluded his use of force had been justified.

entries.title: Trump administration stopped sharing evidence in Good and Pretti killings, Minnesota officials say
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has suggested that state prosecutors don't have jurisdiction to investigate federal officers, while Minnesota officials have said they don't trust the federal government to investigate itself.

entries.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
entries.snippet: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

entries.title: Germany news: Merz calls for unity at CSU party conference

entries.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travels to Chinese border city via newly opened bridge
entries.snippet: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travelled to China’s border city of Dandong via a newly opened bridge linking the two countries, where he met a senior Chinese official.

entries.title: France protests: More violence feared amid renewed demonstrations
entries.snippet: France is deploying some 70,000 police officers as fresh nationwide protests begin. A deadly shooting near Paris has additionally fueled tensions. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Japan-Russia ties erode as journalist sits in Moscow jail
entries.snippet: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

entries.title: Taiwan: Typhoon Champi leaves 1 dead, over 500 injured
entries.snippet: After killing one person and causing major disruptions in Taiwan, Typhoon Champi is now headed towards China.

entries.title: India news: Neha Bora refuses to sign peace bond, cites right to democratic dissent
entries.snippet: Neha Bora says the peace bond violates the right to democratic dissent. The statement comes amid a wider protest calling for the removal of India's election chief. DW has more.

entries.title: Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat catches fire, police say
entries.snippet: Authorities have arrested a suspect as firemen try to put out the fire in Bavaria, near the Austrian border.

entries.title: France to deploy 70,000 police officers ahead of protests
entries.snippet: With new protests in France planned for this weekend, the authorities pledged to do everything in their power to prevent looting, violence and vandalism.

entries.title: Ebola: Kenya announces second death
entries.snippet: Kenyan health officials said the 65-year-old ​woman was a close ‌relative of a ‌​man who died of Ebola last month. The woman developed symptoms ‌while under quarantine in Nairobi.

entries.title: Trump eases Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
entries.snippet: The move comes as Trump's Republican Party scrambles to maintain control of the US Congress, with a Republican candidate in a key Senate race saying she had lobbied to lift the tariffs on Canadian products.

entries.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
entries.snippet: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

entries.title: Jordan: Karak church shooting leaves 7 dead, dozens injured
entries.snippet: A shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan happened during a funeral, according to authorities. Two unidentified men opened fire on the procession, with Jordan's king vowing "the harshest retaliation."

entries.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
entries.snippet: The Ukrainian city of Oleshky, occupied by Russia and on the frontline, faces a humanitarian crisis. The localized truce comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said negotiators would meet for wider talks next month.

entries.title: Afghan women could lose one of their last paths to a higher education
entries.snippet: The US has defunded one of the last universities giving Afghan women the chance to receive an education after the Taliban takeover in 2021. DW spoke with a student who says she's lost hope of ever earning a degree.

entries.title: Romania blames Russia for ship attack in the Black Sea
entries.snippet: Russian strikes against ships attempting to export Ukrainian grain and cargo through the western Black Sea have sharply increased this month.

entries.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
entries.snippet: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

entries.title: Many feared trapped under collapsed building in Nairobi
entries.snippet: People are feared to be trapped after a large, unfinished building in Nairobi collapsed during construction. Rescue operations have proven complicated as police fired tear gas to disperse looters.

entries.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
entries.snippet: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection.
